issuer: the New Brunswick Department of Public Safety's Motor Vehicle Branch, through Service New Brunswick
note: The Government of New Brunswick's driving and licensing pages (read 2026-10-30). The driver's licences page gives its fees 'as of August 1st, 2026': a Class 1-9 licence, valid for four years, at $100 (written test $25, road test $25, not held), and says a Class 5 licence follows a minimum of 24 months at levels 1 and 2 of the Graduated Licence Program, which a person may enter at 16: a full Class 5 licence is kept from 18. The photo identification card page gives the card at $48 to any resident, with no age restriction (so no age is held), and doesn't say how long it lasts (the term is null). The new residents page lets drivers from the Canadian provinces and the United States exchange class for class without a test, and nationals of the countries it lists (Austria, Australia, Belgium, Denmark, England, France, Germany, the Isle of Man, Ireland, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Scotland, the Republic of Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Ukraine and Wales) exchange theirs for a Class 5 without testing: held as every other Canadian province and territory, the 51 US states and DC, every Australian state and territory, and those countries (England, Scotland and Wales as the United Kingdom). Not held: the Taiwan and Ukraine extra papers and vision test, and Prince Edward Island's and Nova Scotia's no-fee exchange.

sources.title: Government of New Brunswick, Driver's licences
sources.said: A person may apply for a Class 7 driver's licence (Graduated Licence Program) at age 16 with parental consent. ... A person may apply for a class 5 driver’s licence, after completing a minimum of 24 months at level 1 and 2 (combined), with a minimum of 12 months in level 2. ... Fees as of August 1st, 2026 ... Class 1-9 Licence is valid for four years $100

sources.title: Government of New Brunswick, Photo identification card
sources.said: Any resident of New Brunswick may apply for a photo identification card. There is no age restriction. ... Photo ID $48.00

sources.title: Government of New Brunswick, Driver's licences for new residents
sources.said: Drivers from Canadian provinces or the United States may exchange their licence class for class, including Class 7, without taking any driver’s test or submitting a medical ... The countries below have reciprocity with Canada and their nationals can exchange their licence without testing for a Class 5 or motorcycle ... Austria, Australia, Belgium, Denmark, England, France, Germany, Isle of Man, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Netherlands (Holland), New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Scotland, Republic of Korea (South Korea), Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan*, Ukraine* and Wales.
